title: Annual time-use categories move modestly while gender and life-stage ordering remains visible
source_unit: ATUS respondent age 15+ with one selected diary day and final/replicate weights

household_work_minutes.unit: weighted mean primary-activity minutes per diary day

care_for_people_minutes.unit: weighted mean primary-activity minutes per diary day

work_minutes.unit: weighted mean primary-activity minutes per diary day

travel_minutes.unit: weighted mean primary-activity minutes per diary day

socializing_communicating_minutes.unit: weighted mean primary-activity minutes per diary day

secondary_childcare_minutes.unit: weighted mean secondary-childcare minutes per diary day

eldercare_minutes.unit: weighted mean eldercare minutes per diary day

observations.method: Official BLS ATUS 2024 respondent, activity, activity-summary, and replicate-weight files; activity rows aggregated by TUCASEID and final-weighted, with 160-replicate standard errors.
observations.uncertainty: Annual population estimate with design-based replicate standard errors; 2024 and 2025 are separate annual samples and are not a respondent-level panel.
observations.subgroup: All valid merged ATUS respondents age 15+.
observations.counterinterpretation: A change between annual samples can reflect composition, diary-day mix, sampling variation, or real population movement; it does not identify a cause.

observations.method: Same BLS ATUS procedure and activity definitions as the 2024 observation, applied to the 2025 annual files.
observations.uncertainty: Annual population estimate with design-based replicate standard errors; no matched respondents or causal timing are claimed.
observations.subgroup: All valid merged ATUS respondents age 15+.
observations.counterinterpretation: The modest category movements may reflect sample composition, diary-day mix, coding or seasonal differences, or real change; they do not establish a societal cause.

boundary: This is a repeated annual population comparison, not a panel of the same respondents. It preserves separate time currencies and uncertainty but does not establish that price, work rules, care needs, technology, or policy caused the annual movements.
